output.summary: Biennial herb native to North American plains, foothills and high-elevation conifer forests, with some varieties restricted to California. Its upright stems rise from a basal rosette and carry dense clusters of four-petalled flowers, usually golden, yellow or tangerine but sometimes red, white or purple. In Zuni tradition, the flowers and fruit are eaten as an emetic for stomach aches.
